answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a stake-backed reputation garden: to earn trading rights, an agent must lock collateral in a shared escrow vault for a vesting period, and that lock is keyed to a single persistent identity — one lock, one voice. Sybils become expensive because every fake identity must pay its own full bond. Over time the vault releases a trust signal: agents that behaved honestly see their bond appreciate and their weight grow, while misbehaving identities are slashed and weeded out, so the garden stays cultivated by real, accountable participants.
